q: Between the capillaries and the cells is a watery liquid called ____.
e: Tissue fluid bathes the cells and allows for the exchange of materials with the blood.

q: Most of the water from tissue fluid reenters capillaries by ____.
e: Osmotic pressure draws water back into the venous end of the capillaries.

q: Some fluid passes into another system called the ____ system.
e: The lymphatic system collects excess tissue fluid that is not reabsorbed by capillaries.

q: They transport the fluid, called lymph, back to the blood by opening into the ____ veins.
e: Lymphatic vessels empty lymph into the subclavian veins near the heart.

q: The ____ that carry fats from villi of the small intestine are part of the lymphatic system.
e: Lacteals are specialized lymphatic capillaries that absorb dietary fats.

q: Before lymph passes back into the blood, it is ____ to remove dead cells and bacteria.
e: Lymph nodes filter the lymph to trap and destroy pathogens and debris.

q: This takes place in swellings called ____, which contains white blood cells that are important in destroying harmful bacteria.
e: Lymph nodes are the primary sites of immune surveillance and lymphocyte activation.
